literature.abstract: Epileptic diathesis is an inherited neurophysiological trait that contributes to the development of all types of epilepsy. Our aim was to explore the amount and topographic distribution of theta activity in epilepsy groups. We hypothesized that the anatomical distribution of increased theta activity is independent of the epilepsy type.

literature.title: Graves'-Basedow's disease--asthma association. Presentation of five cases.
literature.abstract: Thyroid hormones have a non-selective permissive action on adrenergic receptors (including beta 2). Asthma is an immune disease in which some pathological pathways include beta 2 adrenergic receptor blockade. In theoretical terms, that would mean that in hyperthyroidism asthma would ameliorate. In 5 cases with Graves-Basedow's disease--asthma association this phenomenon has not appeared. The similar clinical features and follow-up of these patients suggest a narrow etiopathogenic group.
